candidates.title: Laravel CSV export of deals/leads/contacts/organizations/orders does not neutralise spreadsheet formulas
candidates.description: GET /api/v1/export (SalesController::exportCsv) writes tenant-controlled text fields into CSV cells that are only double-quote escaped. A value such as =HYPERLINK(...) or @SUM(...) is stored raw and evaluated as a formula when a privileged user (holding export.data) opens the file in Excel or Sheets. Lower-privileged writers can plant the value, including anonymous submitters through public lead forms (leads.title, contact_name, email, phone, source) and any role with crm.write. The Worker twin and ReportsController already neutralise formulas, so the Laravel production exporter is inconsistent with the stated intent.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The $esc closure in SalesController::exportCsv does not prefix cells that start with = + - @ tab or CR. ReportsController::csvCell and the Worker deals.ts esc both apply this control.

trace.description: Selects raw user-controlled columns for the tenant; a lower-trust writer controls these values.
The closure only wraps the cell in quotes and doubles embedded quotes; no leading-character check.
CSV served as an attachment with unneutralised cells; formula executes when a privileged user opens it in a spreadsheet.

evidence.description: csvCell shows the intended control: regex on ^[=+\-@\t\r] adds an apostrophe prefix.
Worker twin prefixes an apostrophe when the cell starts with = + - or @.

validation_plan.local: PHPUnit feature test with two dummy tenants. Insert a lead with title '=HYPERLINK("http://example.invalid","x")' and a contact with first_name '@SUM(1+1)' into tenant A. Call GET /api/v1/export?kind=leads and kind=contacts as a tenant_owner of tenant A. Assert no cell begins with = + - or @ after the opening quote. Also assert tenant B rows are absent.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner opens a CSV exported from a dummy tenant containing such a value in a spreadsheet application and observes whether the formula is evaluated or a warning is shown. Do not use real data.

hardening: CrmExtrasController::downloadAttachment (255-262) and WorkspaceController::files require only auth and tenant membership; no read permission check on the parent record type. Tenant isolation holds; role-granularity gap. Map entity_type to its read permission.
Attachment quota check (CrmExtrasController 235-239) is a non-atomic sum-then-insert; overshoot by about one request per concurrent worker.
Upload extension allowlist trusts the client filename extension; no content scanning. Download forces octet-stream with nosniff.
Laravel exportCsv does not call H::requireTenant before using ctx->tenantId.
Worker deals.ts esc omits tab and CR in its formula-prefix regex, unlike ReportsController::csvCell.
In exportCsv the kind value is allowlisted before use in Content-Disposition; no header injection.
